claims.text: The target alloy is a multiprincipal BCC high-entropy alloy.
Short-range atomic disorder and local structural fluctuations enhance electron-phonon coupling at low temperature.
Disorder-enhanced electron-phonon coupling enables superconductivity and raises Tc relative to more ordered states.
The proposed starting specimen has at least five constituent elements and uncharacterized superconducting properties.
An uncharacterized (TaNb)0.67(HfZrTi)0.33-like alloy is an example of the proposed starting state.
Annealing relative to the as-cast state systematically reduces short-range disorder.
Pressure up to about 30 GPa can be used to track structural evolution and superconductivity in the proposed comparison.
Short-range chemical order and local bonding distortions are the structural mediators linking processing or pressure to superconductivity.
Local disruptions caused by multiple principal elements broaden the phonon spectrum.
The broadened phonon spectrum strengthens electron-phonon coupling.
Stronger electron-phonon coupling raises Tc in more disordered alloy states.
As-cast specimens have greater short-range disorder than annealed specimens.
As-cast specimens will have slightly higher Tc than annealed specimens under matched conditions.
More-disordered as-cast specimens will retain superconductivity over a broader pressure range than more-ordered annealed specimens.
Heat-treated materials with reduced short-range disorder will have modestly lower Tc under the same temperature-pressure conditions.
The hypothesized effect applies to minimally contaminated multiprincipal BCC alloys containing at least five elements, below 15 K and up to about 30 GPa.
Outside the specified pressure, temperature, composition, and crystal-structure regime, the disorder effect may weaken or change.
Compositional inhomogeneity, alternative pairing mechanisms, and preparation or measurement differences could obscure the proposed disorder-Tc relationship.
Failure to observe a consistent positive relationship between measured local disorder and Tc would falsify the hypothesis.
